headline: Yearly prices up 13% to 20% on Grow and Advanced
what: Shopify's pricing page now shows pay-yearly prices of $89/mo for Grow (was $79) and $359/mo for Advanced (was $299). Pay-monthly prices are unchanged at $105 and $399, and Basic is unchanged at $29 yearly / $39 monthly. That cuts the annual-billing discount from about 25% to about 15% on Grow and about 10% on Advanced, and raises a year of Grow from $948 to $1,068 and a year of Advanced from $3,588 to $4,308.
who: Shopify merchants on Grow or Advanced who pay yearly or are about to renew or sign up on annual billing
seo_title: Shopify raised annual prices: Grow now $89/mo, Advanced $359/mo (pricing update)
seo_desc: Shopify's pay-yearly prices rose to $89/mo for Grow (from $79) and $359/mo for Advanced (from $299). Monthly prices are unchanged, so the annual discount shrank to roughly 10-15%.
note: Update (Oct 19, 2026): on October 19, Shopify's pricing page showed the older $79/mo Grow and $299/mo Advanced yearly prices again, and repeated checks returned both versions (six of ten checks showed $79/$299, four showed $89/$359). The higher yearly prices look like a price test shown to some visitors rather than a completed increase. See our Oct 19 update.

headline: Enterprise+ now has a public price: $45 per user
what: Slack's pricing page used to say "Contact sales for pricing" for Enterprise+. It now lists $45 USD per user per month when paying annually, with the Contact Sales button still shown.
who: Organizations evaluating or negotiating Slack Enterprise+ plans
seo_title: Slack Enterprise+ price is now public: $45 per user per month (annual)
seo_desc: Slack's pricing page now lists Enterprise+ at $45 per user per month billed annually, replacing the old 'Contact sales for pricing' line.
note: Update (Oct 18, 2026): on Oct 18, Slack's pricing page alternated between showing the $45 Enterprise+ price and "Contact sales for pricing" across repeated checks, so the public price appears to be shown to some visitors and not others. On Oct 19 the page again showed $45 in our morning snapshot, and later checks still returned both versions.

headline: Claude Enterprise now lists a 20-seat minimum
what: The Enterprise plan on Anthropic's pricing page still reads US$20/seat/month billed annually plus usage at API rates, but now adds "20 seat minimum." That implies at least $4,800 a year in seat fees before any usage.
who: Small companies and teams considering Claude Enterprise instead of the Team plan
seo_title: Claude Enterprise now requires 20 seats minimum (Anthropic pricing update)
seo_desc: Anthropic's pricing page now says Claude Enterprise is US$20/seat/month billed annually with a 20 seat minimum, plus usage at API rates.

headline: New Figma Specs beta added to paid seats
what: Figma's pricing page adds Figma Specs, a beta for writing structured specs on the canvas, available on paid seats. Full, Dev, and Collab seat descriptions now all include Figma Specs, and Full seats now explicitly list Figma Motion. Figma Make also gains secrets management and a scaffolded Payload backend (database, APIs, auth, admin panel).
who: Figma customers on paid Full, Dev, or Collab seats

headline: Annual plans: cancellation now effective next billing cycle
what: Audible's plan page now says its annual Premium plans ($149.50/yr for 12 credits, $229.50/yr for 24 credits) can be canceled anytime "effective next billing cycle," where it previously just said "Cancel anytime." The "Save 16%" labels on the annual plans were also removed. Prices did not change.
who: Audible members on, or considering, annual Premium plans
note: Correction (Oct 15, 2026): a later check of the live Audible plans page still showed "Cancel anytime" and the "Save 16%" labels on annual plans. We could not confirm that those phrases were removed or that cancellation wording changed to "effective next billing cycle."

headline: Narrows error and fraud protection for linked external-account transactions (Oct 19)
what: Bank of America's new Online Banking Service Agreement takes effect October 19, 2026, replacing the August 27, 2026 version. The prior text gave customers 90 days to report errors or unauthorized activity "if the problem or error relates to a transfer from an account maintained at another financial institution." The new text keeps that 90-day window only for Bill Pay payments funded from an outside account to an outside, third-party payee. It adds: "Except for transfers initiated through the Bill Pay Service that are funded from an account maintained at another financial institution ('External Account')… Bank of America is not responsible for investigating or resolving errors or other disputes for electronic transactions that appear on your External Account statement." A related line says the unauthorized-transaction protections in Section 8.B "apply only to accounts maintained with Bank of America," with the same Bill Pay exception. Paying a BofA card or loan from a linked Chase or credit-union account now means taking most disputes to that other bank.
who: Bank of America online and mobile banking customers who link accounts at other banks, especially those who pay BofA credit cards, mortgages, or HELOCs from an outside account
seo_title: Bank of America's new online banking agreement limits disputes on linked external accounts (Oct 19, 2026)
seo_desc: From Oct 19, BofA says it won't investigate errors on transactions that show on your other bank's statement, except Bill Pay. The 90-day window shrinks too.

headline: Regulatory Charge rises 24% to $0.26 per voice line on Nov 1
what: Verizon's surcharges support page now states: "Effective November 1, 2026, the monthly Verizon Wireless Regulatory Charge for voice-capable devices will increase from $0.21 to $0.26 per line." That is a 24% jump on one of Verizon's own mobile surcharges (not a government tax). Combined with the unchanged Administrative and Telco Recovery Charge ($3.78 per voice line), Verizon's two flat per-line surcharge lines go from $3.99 to $4.04. Separately, Verizon disclosures show the Federal Universal Service Charge using a 42% factor, matching the FCC's Q4 2026 contribution factor (DA-26-946), the program's highest on record after 38.8% in Q3.
who: Verizon postpaid wireless customers with voice-capable lines; federal USF percentage-based charges affect wireless bills industry-wide
seo_title: Verizon price increase 2026: fees rise to $4.95 a line (Regulatory Charge Nov 1, admin charge $4.69 Nov 15)
seo_desc: Verizon's Regulatory Charge goes from $0.21 to $0.26 per voice line on Nov 1, 2026, and its Administrative and Telco Recovery Charge from $3.78 to $4.69 on Nov 15.
note: October 23, 2026: Verizon's Important Plan Information page (figures as of October 1, 2026) now also lists a bigger increase: the Administrative and Telco Recovery Charge goes from $3.78 to $4.69 per voice line on November 15, 2026 (+$0.91). With the Regulatory Charge change, Verizon's two flat per-line surcharges go from $3.99 to $4.04 on November 1 and to $4.95 on November 15. Data-only lines stay at $3.97 plus $0.02. The myPlan 3-year price lock excludes surcharges, so it doesn't stop either increase. How it compares (each carrier's own page, checked October 23, 2026): T-Mobile charges a Regulatory Programs & Telco Recovery Fee of "$5.49 per line every month" on voice lines (plans that bill fees separately), and AT&T's Mobility fee schedule lists its Administrative & Regulatory Cost Recovery Fee at "$4.99 per line per month." After November 15, Verizon's $4.95 sits between the two. On a four-line Verizon account the two flat charges go from $15.96 to $19.80 a month, $3.84 more, or about $46 a year, before universal service charges and taxes.
sources: Verizon, Important Plan Information ($4.69 effective Nov 15, 2026)
T-Mobile, Your bill and what's impacting it ($5.49 per voice line)
AT&T, Wireless fee schedule ($4.99 per line per month)
faq: How much is Verizon raising its fees in November 2026?

Two Verizon surcharges go up for each voice line. The Regulatory Charge goes from $0.21 to $0.26 on November 1, 2026, and the Administrative and Telco Recovery Charge goes from $3.78 to $4.69 on November 15, 2026. Together they rise from $3.99 to $4.95 a line each month.
Does the myPlan price lock protect me from the increase?
No. Verizon's 3-year myPlan price lock covers the plan price but excludes surcharges like the Administrative and Telco Recovery Charge and the Regulatory Charge, so both increases still apply.
How much more will a family plan pay?
On a four-line account, the two flat surcharges go from $15.96 to $19.80 a month, which is $3.84 more a month or about $46 a year, before universal service charges and taxes.
How do Verizon's fees compare with AT&T and T-Mobile?

As of October 23, 2026, T-Mobile charges $5.49 per voice line for its Regulatory Programs & Telco Recovery Fee, and AT&T charges $4.99 per line for its Administrative & Regulatory Cost Recovery Fee. After November 15, Verizon's $4.95 sits just below AT&T.

headline: Airline delay-category rule pushed to Feb 1, 2027 (flights from Jan 1)
what: A Federal Register notice published October 15, 2026 (FR Doc 2026-21058) delays the effective date of DOT's September 3, 2026 final rule on airline delay and cancellation categories under Section 511(b) of the FAA Reauthorization Act. The rule, which creates a new category for ten events that will no longer count as "Air Carrier" (controllable) delays or cancellations—including certain unscheduled maintenance, removing an unruly passenger, medical emergencies, cyberattacks, and government system failures—now takes effect February 1, 2027 instead of October 19, 2026. The new categories apply to flights on or after January 1, 2027, so holiday-season flights stay under the old categories. DOT's earlier analysis said the change is expected to reduce the number of delays and cancellations for which carriers provide amenities and compensation under voluntary commitments.
who: U.S. air travelers; meal and hotel help still depends on each airline's voluntary customer-service commitments
seo_title: DOT delays airline "controllable delay" change to Feb 1, 2027: maintenance, medical, unruly-passenger delays
seo_desc: The DOT rule taking 10 delay causes, including unscheduled maintenance, out of airline-caused categories now applies to flights from Jan 1, 2027, not Oct 19.
